s: I ___ a silly mistake in the report.
note: We make mistakes, but we do homework.

s: Please ___ your homework before dinner.
note: Homework, chores and work take 'do'.

s: Can you ___ me a favour and post this letter?
note: A favour is something you do for someone.

s: We have been working for two hours; let's ___ a break.
note: 'Have a break' is also fine; 'do a break' is not English.

s: Please ___ attention to the safety instructions.
note: Attention is something you pay, as if it costs you effort.

s: Can you ___ a secret?
note: We keep secrets, promises and appointments.

s: I ran but could not ___ the 8:15 local.
note: You catch a train, bus or flight when you reach it in time.

s: Ananya ___ a cold after getting wet in the rain.
note: You catch a cold, as if it flew to you.

s: Meena ___ an important question at the meeting.
note: Raise takes an object; rise does not. You raise a question.

s: We should not ___ conclusions without enough data.
note: We draw conclusions, the way we draw water from a well.

s: After four hours, the two sides ___ an agreement.
note: Arrive needs 'at'; reach takes the object directly.

s: Our team ___ the deadline with a day to spare.
note: You meet or miss a deadline; you complete the work.

s: My cousin ___ a small bakery in Pune.
note: You run a shop, a company or a project.

s: The college will ___ a meeting on Friday.
note: Formal events are held: meetings, elections, talks.

s: Please ___ on the light; it is dark in here.
note: 'Open the light' is common in India but confuses others. Lights are switched or turned on.

s: Kabir will ___ his maths exam on Monday.
note: 'Give an exam' is common in India, but elsewhere the examiner gives it. Students take or sit it.

s: We had ___ rain all night, and the streets flooded.
note: Rain is heavy or light, never big.

s: I need a cup of ___ coffee to wake up.
note: Tea and coffee are strong or weak.

s: The child has a ___ fever, so we are taking her to the doctor.
note: Fever and temperature are high, not big.

s: I am ___ sorry for the delay in replying.
note: Deeply goes with feelings: deeply sorry, deeply moved, deeply hurt.

s: The fans were ___ disappointed by the last-ball loss.
note: Bitterly is the natural partner of disappointed, cold and regret.

s: It is ___ unlikely that the match will start on time.
note: Highly goes with likely, unlikely, probable and successful.

s: I am ___ aware of the risks of this plan.
note: Fully aware means you know everything about it.

s: I ___ disagree with the decision to cut the library budget.
note: 'Highly disagree' is a common mistake; we strongly agree or disagree.

s: The scooter missed us by inches; it was a ___ escape.
note: A narrow escape means you only just avoided danger.

s: I have only a ___ idea of how the new tax works.
note: Vague means unclear; blurry is for pictures and eyesight.

s: There is a ___ chance of rain tomorrow.
note: Slight or small chance; rain can be light, a chance cannot.

s: The instructions were ___ clear, so nobody got lost.
note: Crystal clear means completely clear, with no doubt at all.

s: She gave us a ___ smile when she saw the results.
note: A broad smile is a wide, happy one.

s: There has been a ___ rise in petrol prices this month.
note: Sharp or steep rise means sudden and large.

s: Let me ___ a look at your code before you submit it.
note: 'Take a look' also works; 'do a look' does not.

s: Please don't ___ a noise; the baby is sleeping.
note: We make noise, make a sound, make a fuss.

s: Dr Iyer ___ a speech at the annual day function.
note: You give or make a speech; you say words and speak at a function.

s: We should ___ a party for Dadi's eightieth birthday.
note: Throw or have a party; 'make a party' is a common slip.

s: Please ___ a seat; the doctor will see you soon.
note: 'Have a seat' is also polite; 'sit a seat' is not English.

s: Rahul ___ his promise and came to the wedding.
note: You keep or break a promise.

s: Zoya ___ a good impression at the interview.
note: You make an impression on someone.

s: Are you ready to ___ the risk of starting your own firm?
note: We take risks and take chances.

s: Please ___ me a call when you land in Chennai.
note: Give me a call is friendly; 'make me a call' is not used.

s: Doctors have ___ the alarm about rising dengue cases.
note: Raise the alarm means warn people about danger.
